narrative.overview:
The ITSD Project Tracker embodies the authority of a well-maintained ledger — dense, trustworthy, and unambiguous. Every element earns its place through function, not decoration. The system presents portfolio delivery data with the precision of architectural drafting: framework color spines anchor vertical rhythm, metric zones differentiate from identity zones through tonal contrast, and status communication happens through color-coded badges that read at a glance.

The aesthetic is document-forward: near-white drafting-paper ground, near-black technical ink hierarchy, and a restrained institutional blue reserved for interactive state. Density is a feature — the dashboard fits an entire portfolio in one view without losing scannability. The visual language says: this is the system of record.
keyCharacteristics: Architectural drafting aesthetic with framework color spines
Dense data tables with metric zone / identity zone differentiation
Tonal layering over shadows for depth hierarchy
Restrained accent blue for interactive state only
Status communication through semantic color badges

rules.name: The Accent Restraint Rule
rules.body: Institutional Blue appears on ≤15% of any given viewport. It marks interactive state only — links, focus rings, selected filters, primary buttons.

rules.name: The Status Pairing Rule
rules.body: Status and health colors always appear as bg+ink pairs. Never use the ink color alone without its background tint.

rules.name: The Tabular Nums Rule
rules.body: All numeric columns in data tables use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for vertical alignment.

rules.name: The Label Caps Rule
rules.body: Column headers and section labels use: 10px, 600 weight, 0.08em letter-spacing, uppercase.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Tonal differentiation does the depth work. Shadows appear only as response to state.

rules.name: The Tonal Layering Rule
rules.body: Depth is communicated through background value, not shadow. ground → ground-metric → surface progression implies lift.

rules.name: The Spine Rule
rules.body: Every framework section begins with its 6px color spine. The spine is the primary visual anchor.

dos: Do use the framework color spine on every framework section
Do use tabular-nums for all numeric columns in data tables
Do use label-caps style for column headers and section labels
Do use status bg+ink pairs together — never separate them
Do use ground-metric to differentiate metric zones from identity zones
Do keep accent blue to interactive elements only (links, focus, selected state)
donts: Don't use accent blue for decorative purposes or section backgrounds
Don't add shadows to cards or panels at rest — keep them flat
Don't use body text style for headers — always use label-caps
Don't round framework sections or tables — keep them sharp
Don't use status colors for non-semantic purposes (decoration, emphasis)
Don't add breathing room beyond the spacing scale — density is a feature
